subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Key Risk Indicators
description: A short lesson to help you apply Key Risk Indicators.

hook.text: Staff turnover spikes. System downtime increases. Complaint volumes triple. These are warning signs.

buildup.text: Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) are measurable metrics that signal rising operational risk before losses occur.

discovery.text: Common KRIs include error rates, staff turnover, audit findings, system outages, and customer complaints.

twist.text: KRIs only work if thresholds are set right. Too sensitive and you drown in noise. Too loose and you miss real signals.

climax.text: KRIs are the early warning system for operational risk. They don't prevent problems but they give you time.

punchline.text: Watch the indicators. They warn before the losses hit.

quiz.question: What is a Key Risk Indicator?
options: A metric that signals rising risk before losses occur
